identity.mechanic: Changelings wear other units' text. Each one has small stats and a small text of its own, plus one borrowed **Guise**. A Guise can come from the shop, from your own board, from a unit you sell, or from the enemy across. A second verb, **Exchange**, swaps one of your units with a unit in the shop, so the tribe trades with the shop as well as buying from it.

keywords.name: Guise
keywords.text:
A Changeling can wear one other unit's Guise. That means the unit's own text (as it stands, golden if that unit is golden) and its tribe, on top of the Changeling's own. Stats are never copied unless a card says so.
- A new Guise replaces the old one.
- **One of each:** no two of your Changelings wear the same unit's Guise. If one takes a Guise another already wears, the other loses it.
- A Guise taken while recruiting stays on the card wherever it goes: hand, shop, or flying south. If the Changeling wears it when played, the Guise's "When played" fires too. A Guise taken in a fight ends with the fight, and the earlier Guise comes back.
- **Fires at once:** a Guise taken by a "When played" or a "Start of Combat" fires that same trigger straight away, right after the text that gave it. A Guise whose own text takes a Guise doesn't fire this way.
- **Kept:** a Changeling kept its Guise this turn if it wears one at End of Turn and didn't change it this turn. A Guise first taken when it was played this turn counts as kept.
- A Guise copies a unit's own text, never that unit's Guise. It never copies a Tier 6 unit.

keywords.name: Exchange
keywords.text: Put a friendly unit into the shop in place of a shop unit you choose, and take that shop unit into your hand (you need a free hand space). The swap is fair: the new unit counts as Bought if you gave a Bought unit, and as Created otherwise. Until the shop refreshes you can buy back the unit you gave, with its buffs and Guise, at the normal price. After a refresh it goes back to the pool as a plain copy; a Stock or other token is removed instead.

identity.plays: A Changeling player is a guest in someone else's tribe. Early on you pick up a Kit and a Hob and borrow the best text in the shop or on your board. In the middle game you decide whether to keep your Guises, which pays over time, or keep swapping them, which pays each time. You also decide whether to work the shop with Exchanges. Because a Guise brings its tribe with it, Changelings count as Birds, Oozes or Hedgerow folk for those tribes' own cards. The best Changeling board is two tribes at once. Late on, the Lady Under the Hill wears all of your Guises at once, the Fetch copies your carry for each fight, and Bettie Underhill pays out for every Exchange you made this game.

units.name: Cradle Kit
units.text: When played: take the Guise of a unit in the shop. Its "When played" fires now too.
units.golden: 4/4. The Guise it takes is golden.

units.name: Weeks-Old Hob
units.text: When played: take the Guise of a unit beside it. End of Turn: if this kept its Guise this turn, gain +1/+1 permanently.

units.name: Clerk of Exchanges
units.text: When played: Exchange a friendly unit.
units.golden: 4/6. Exchange up to two friendly units.

units.name: Veil-Stitcher
units.text: End of Turn: give your Changelings that wear a Guise +1/+1 permanently.

units.name: Pip Unlike
units.text: When played: take the Guise of a friendly unit, mirror-backwards: in its text, left and right swap, and so do in front of and behind.

units.name: Turncoat Hare
units.text: Start of Combat: take the Guise of the enemy across for this fight. Its "Start of Combat" fires now too.

units.name: Wicker Moll
units.text: Once a turn, when you sell or Exchange away a unit: leave a Stock in its slot, wearing that unit's Guise.

units.name: Grandfer Acorn
units.text: Whenever a friendly Changeling takes a Guise while recruiting, it gains +2/+1 permanently.

units.name: Counter Stand-In
units.text: Whenever you sell a unit, this may take its Guise.

units.name: Tam Twice
units.text: Wears two Guises at once. When played: take the Guises of two other friendly units. (This text can't be worn as a Guise.)

units.name: Matron of the Exchange Room
units.text: End of Turn: for each tribe among your units, give a random unit of that tribe +2/+2 permanently. (A Changeling counts as its Guise's tribe too.)

units.name: Placement Officer
units.text: Start of Turn: you may Exchange a friendly unit. If it wore a Guise, that Guise moves to the unit you take, which becomes a Changeling too.
units.golden: 6/10. Up to two, each moving its Guise.

units.name: Coat-Peg Steward
units.text: Whenever you Exchange, the unit you give loses the permanent stats it had gained, and the unit you take gains them, plus +2/+2.

units.name: Long-Stay Hollin
units.text: End of Turn: each friendly Changeling that kept its Guise this turn gains +1/+1 permanently for each Tier of the unit it copies.

units.name: Penny Second
units.text: Start of Combat: take the Guise of the enemy across for this fight; its "Start of Combat" fires now too. Then, if this is bigger than it, that enemy loses its text for this fight.

units.name: Keeper of the Lost Hour
units.text: Your Changelings' Guise text that triggers in a fight triggers twice. Extra copies of this text, played or worn, add nothing; only the best one counts.

units.name: The Lady Under the Hill
units.text: Wears every Guise your other Changelings wear (not other copies of this text). One of each doesn't apply to her. Her Guises never count as taking or keeping a Guise.

units.name: The Fetch
units.text: Start of Combat: make a Stock in the empty slot nearest this, for this fight. It copies your biggest other unit: its stats, its own text as a Guise, and any Guises it wears. One of each doesn't apply to the Stock. (A Tier 6 unit gives only its stats.)
units.golden: 12/16. Two Stocks, copying your two biggest other units.

units.name: Bettie Underhill
units.text: End of Turn: give your Changelings +1/+1 permanently for each Exchange you've made this game.

extras.name: Stock
extras.text: A 1/3 Changeling, Created, with no text of its own. It can wear a Guise like any Changeling. *(Wicker Moll's sigh in their sleep.)*

extras.name: Midnight Swap
extras.text: (price 2). Exchange a friendly unit. Any tribe can use it while Changelings are in the lobby.

builds.name: The Masquerade (Guise bridge)
builds.text: Cradle Kit, Pip, Counter Stand-In, Tam Twice and Grandfer Acorn, building to the Lady and the Keeper of the Lost Hour. You pick a second tribe from the lobby and wear its best texts. A Kit wearing a Bird's Guise is a Bird, so selling it sends it south and it comes home with doubled stats, still in its Guise. With Hedgerow folk, Pip mirrors "Pass X: your rightmost other unit" into a leftmost pass, so you get a second pass lane. A Changeling wearing an Ooze's Belly holds units like an Ooze. The Matron grows with each tribe your Guises bring. The Lady then holds all those texts in one body: Belly, Mire and Pass on one 7/7.

builds.name: The Board of Exchanges (shop swap)
builds.text:
Clerk of Exchanges, Midnight Swap, Wicker Moll, Placement Officer and Coat-Peg Steward, building to Bettie Underhill. Exchange a spent or small unit for the shop's best each turn. Moll leaves a Stock in its slot that keeps the old unit's text, the Steward moves the old unit's buffs onto the new one, and the Officer moves its Guise. Off-label uses:
- Exchange a buffed unit away and **freeze**: the shop holds it as an eighth slot until you buy it back.
- Buy it back to replay its "When played".
- Exchange a 0-value Stock to get a free shop unit.

Bettie pays once for each Exchange in the game, so starting early matters.

builds.name: The Long Swap (keepers)
builds.text: Weeks-Old Hob, Veil-Stitcher, Long-Stay Hollin and the Matron. Put high-tier Guises on early and never change them. A Kit played at Tier 5 copies a Tier 5 shop unit, and Hollin then pays +5/+5 a turn for it. This pulls against Grandfer and the Stand-In, which pay for changing Guises. Choosing between keeping and swapping is the tribe's main decision in the middle game.

builds.name: Impostors (fight copying)
builds.text: Turncoat Hare, Penny Second, the Keeper and the Fetch. You can see your next opponent's last board, so you place Turncoat and Penny across their key unit. Against Bog folk, Penny takes the Mire unit's text, the enemy loses its Mire, and Penny holds the Mire instead. Against Hunters, Penny takes the Quarry text. The Keeper fires stolen Start of Combat text twice. The Fetch makes a copy of your carry for each fight, its text and Guises included, if you keep a slot empty for it. A Tier 6 carry gives only its stats.

risks: **Reading the board.** A Changeling has two texts, Tam has three and the Lady can have five or more. The UI has to show a Guise as a compact second line or a tag, or Changeling boards become unreadable. This is the biggest look-and-feel cost.

**Borrowed economy.** A Guise of a neutral gold unit doubles that gold. The one-of-each rule caps it at one extra copy, plus the Lady. If it is still too much, gold text pays half when worn as a Guise.
**Strength depends on the lobby.** Changelings are only as good as the other tribes and neutrals that roll. In a weak lobby the tribe has low stats and borrows little.
**Weak identity.** Players may feel they are playing someone else's tribe. The Changeling payoffs (Grandfer, Veil-Stitcher, Hollin, Bettie) are there to keep the tribe the owner of the board.
**Hand space.** A full hand blocks an Exchange. Players may find this annoying at Start of Turn with the Placement Officer.
**Penny's silence** can feel bad for the player who loses their key text. It hits one unit, needs Penny to be the bigger unit, and is visible from the recorded board.
**Stock clutter.** Moll can fill the board with weak 1/3 Stocks. They sell for 0 and make good Exchange fodder, but a board left full of Stocks loses fights.
**Rules edges.** These need playtests: Guises firing at once when taken, fight Guises giving way to recruit Guises, Exchanged units in a frozen shop, the Lady with the Fetch.
**The Keeper and the Lady** together are the high roll. The Keeper only doubles fight triggers, and Tier 6 text can't be copied, so it stays inside a fight.

tier_check.note: Bodies 4 and 4, at the median. The Kit's borrowed text is about one T1 card's text, once (target ~1). The Hob gives +2 stats a turn, about 0.5 body (target 0.4). That is slightly over, but it needs a Guise kept all turn.

Bodies 5, below the median of 6 on purpose, because the Guise or Exchange text is worth a second card. The Clerk is worth about 2 gold once, about 1 body. The Veil-Stitcher gives 4–6 stats a turn with 2–3 Guised units (0.7–1 body, at the top of the range). Pip is a once-off copy.

Bodies 7, at the median. Grandfer gives about 6 a turn at two Guises a turn (0.85 body). Moll gives a 1/3 Stock plus a kept text a turn (~0.8). Turncoat gives a copied enemy text for one fight (~1 body in fight). The Stand-In gives a text per sell.

Bodies 8–9. The Matron gives 12–16 a turn across 3–4 tribes (1.4–1.9 bodies). That is slightly over because it needs breadth. The Officer is worth about 2 gold a turn, plus a Guise moved onto the unit it brings in. Tam's two Guises match "repeat one" (Kelp Keeper) at this tier. **Broken on purpose:** T4 has both a multiplier (Tam) and an economy piece (Officer), with one buffer, because the Exchange line needs a repeatable source before its T6 payoff.

Bodies 12–13. Hollin gives ~32 a turn with four Changelings at Guise tier 4 (2.7 bodies, above the 2 target, under the top of 5), as the direction card. Penny is a copy plus a silence in fight (~3–4 bodies against a key unit). The Keeper is the Brann slot, narrowed to fight triggers.

Bodies 14–15. Bettie gives ~56 a turn with 7 Exchanges and four Changelings (4 bodies, on target). The Fetch's copy of the carry (stats, text and Guises) is ~6 bodies in fight (on target); a Tier 6 carry gives stats only, so capstones still don't stack. The Lady wears 3–5 texts: a capstone with no fixed number. **Broken on purpose:** a Guise can't copy Tier 6 text, so capstones can't stack. **Runaway check:** No unit's gain feeds its own source: Hollin's pay rests on a fixed tier, and Bettie's on an Exchange count. The first pass found two loops: Bettie copied through Pip, Tam and the Lady (about 800 a turn), and the Keeper doubling End of Turn buffs. Three rules closed them: one of each, no Tier 6 Guises, and fight-only doubling. The worst case left is Hollin worn three ways (~120 a turn), under T6's top. Goldens double a Guise's numbers, which stays inside ×2–4. **v2:** a third loop closed: the Coat-Peg Steward copied stats on round-trip Exchanges (golden: doubling each time). It now moves them, so each round trip adds only +2/+2.

rationale: **Gap: a closed shop.** No tribe interacts with the shop except by buying; Fairies' Rings and Hedgerow's Pass both work only on your own board.
**Gap: no bridge, no counterplay.** Every tribe's keywords feed only itself. No card reads the enemy's text, although the next opponent's board is visible and "across" already exists.

**Guise is the core,** because one verb fills the bridge gap and is the seed's "become what you replace". It copies text and tribe but not stats, so the tribe stays small-bodied and the borrowed text is the value.
**Exchange is the second verb,** to fill the shop gap and put the folklore swap into the rules: a fair trade, with a Stock left in place.
**Exchanged units arrive in hand,** so their "When played" fires and Moll's Stock can take the empty slot.

**Each tier adds a new Guise source,** rather than a bigger number: shop (T1), friend (T1–2), sold unit and enemy (T3), two at once (T4), every Guise (T6). This follows the "more recipients, not bigger packets" rule.
**Keep or swap is the main decision:** Hob and Hollin pay for keeping a Guise, Grandfer and the Stand-In for changing it.
**Penny and Turncoat use the visible next board,** so placing units across the enemy becomes a planning decision. The silence needs Penny to be the bigger unit, so building Penny's stats matters.
**The Matron counts tribes,** so borrowing many tribes pays and the bridge is rewarded, not just allowed.
**The guardrails came out of the runaway pass:** one of each, no Tier 6 Guises, and the Keeper doubling fight triggers only.

changes.what: Guise keyword defines a kept Guise; the Guise taken when played counts as kept that turn.
changes.why: Hob and Hollin said 'kept all turn', which never held on the turn they were played.

changes.what: Pays if it kept its Guise this turn, using the keyword's new Kept rule.
changes.why: Unclear whether the turn it is played counts; now it does.

changes.what: Same Kept wording as Weeks-Old Hob.
changes.why: Same unclear 'kept all turn' for Changelings played this turn.

changes.what: Its text can't be worn as a Guise.
changes.why: A worn Tam Guise asked for two more Guises, and no rule said what happens.

changes.what: Stock copies the biggest other unit's stats, own text and Guises; ignores One of each; Tier 6 gives stats only.
changes.why: Copying a Guise stripped the carry under One of each, and non-Changeling carries gave a blank Stock.

changes.what: The given unit's Guise moves to the unit you take, which becomes a Changeling.
changes.why: It only repeated the Clerk; now Exchange and Guise feed each other.
